title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors, including unauthorized computer access, repeated annoying phone calls, and violating a restraining order. After his mistress ended their relationship, he contacted her thousands of times by text, phone, and social media over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in one day. He also called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in a single day and repeatedly drove past her home.

Josett used the California Law Enforcement Telecommunications System to make 13 unauthorized inquiries about his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and he accessed the police department's license plate reader system to track vehicles. After being served with a protective order and notice of termination on June 28, 2024, he drove by her house and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, and his law enforcement certification review is pending.
